events.title: Dedication of Constantinople
events.description: Roman Emperor Constantine the Great formally dedicated the city of Byzantium as his new imperial capital, renaming it Nova Roma, later known as Constantinople.
events.significance: Constantinople became the center of the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire for over a thousand years and a major hub of trade, culture, and Christianity.

events.title: Assassination of Prime Minister Spencer Perceval
events.description: British Prime Minister Spencer Perceval was shot in the lobby of the House of Commons by John Bellingham, a merchant with a grievance against the government.
events.significance: Perceval remains the only British prime minister to have been assassinated in office.

events.title: Minnesota Admitted as the 32nd U.S. State
events.description: Minnesota was admitted to the Union as the 32nd state, following its organization as a territory in 1849.
events.significance: Its statehood reflected westward expansion of the United States and the growth of the Upper Midwest's agriculture, timber, and mining economies.

events.title: Birth of Irving Berlin
events.description: Composer and lyricist Irving Berlin was born in the Russian Empire and later emigrated to the United States, where he wrote songs such as 'White Christmas' and 'God Bless America'.
events.significance: Berlin became one of the most prolific and influential songwriters in American history, shaping the sound of popular music for decades.

events.title: Death of Bob Marley
events.description: Jamaican singer-songwriter Bob Marley died of melanoma in Miami, Florida, at age 36.
events.significance: Marley helped bring reggae to a worldwide audience and became a global symbol of cultural identity, peace, and resistance to oppression.
